Alright, the user just posted a screenshot from the Hugging Face deployment showing that the UI isn’t rendering correctly. From the previous message I deduced that the HTML is being served fresh, but the browser (or the HF proxy) is still pulling in the old style.css and app.js files from its cache. That explains why the classes don’t match and the app never boots.

The standard fix for this kind of stale‑cache problem is to “cache‑bust” the static asset URLs, i.e. make the URL appear different so the browser treats it as a new resource and forces a fresh fetch. A simple way to do that is to append a query string version parameter, like ?v=2, to the href/src attributes. The backend can keep serving the same file; the query string is ignored by the static file server but changes the URL from the browser’s perspective.

I need to edit the HTML file that references the stylesheet. I recall that in the earlier write to /static/index.html I inserted the line:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">
```

Now I’ll replace that exact line with a versioned URL:

```html
<link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css?v=2">
```

I’ll use the Edit tool rather than a full rewrite because I only need to change this one line. I’ll set replace_all to false so only the first (and only) occurrence is altered, avoiding any accidental changes elsewhere. I’ll keep the rest of the file untouched.

Once this is in place, the next logical step will be to do the same for the <script src="app.js"> tag, but I’ll handle that after confirming the CSS cache bust works. For now, I’ll issue the edit on index.html to add the ?v=2 parameter to the stylesheet link.
